placements.quote: The OPERA detector at the LNGS underground laboratory

summary.plain: A wall of about 150,000 bricks, each a stack of photographic film and lead sheets, arranged with electronic trackers and magnets, deep under Italy's Gran Sasso mountain.
summary.technical: Hybrid emulsion-cloud-chamber detector: about 150,000 emulsion/lead 'bricks' (8.3 kg each) arranged in two supermodules interleaved with plastic-scintillator trigger planes, followed by muon spectrometers, at LNGS Hall C on the CNGS beam line.

technology.quote: The full OPERA target is segmented in about 150 000 bricks arranged in two identical supermodules
technology.value: Lead/nuclear-emulsion 'brick' target-tracker (emulsion cloud chamber) with electronic scintillator trackers and magnetic muon spectrometers
